newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rugby union-Brumbies to gain cash boost.
newsitem.headline: Rugby union-Brumbies to gain cash boost.

text.p: ACT Brumbies have gained a major financial boost to further lift their spirits as they prepare for the Super 12 semifinal against Wellington on Saturday.

The Australian Rugby Union (ARU) has agreed in principle to scrap a player payment system that disadvantaged the Brumbies to the tune of A$1.6 million compared to Queensland and New South Wales when the code turned professional in 1995.
If the proposal is adopted, all three states will have the same amount of money to spend on putting together a squad of players.
"The acceptance of this concept will go a long way towards ensuring that there are three competitive Super 12 teams," ARU chief executive officer John O'Neill said in a statement.
"Each (state) would receive an equal sum of money which is designed to achieve fairness and equity between the participants, particularly in the competition for player talent," he said.
"Payments above an agreed level, which largely will reflect Wallaby duties, will be paid by the ARU."
Previously, the ARU directly contracted and paid 25 elite Wallaby players before dividing the remaining available money between the states.
The situation worked against ACT because only scrumhalf George Gregan and winger Joe Roff were contracted by ARU, forcing them to divide their grant between more than 20 players.
With the ARU picking up about half their wage bill, Queensland and New South Wales, in contrast, had the same amount of money to spend on about half as many players.
